author: menu-architecture
purpose: Proposes the complete top menu bar architecture for the Handshake Studio module, sized against parsed captures of the real applications. Authority stays in the WP-KERNEL-STUDIO microtask contracts and Master Spec section 14; this file is a proposal.
naming_law: STU-SECTION-003: no vendor product name is a Studio menu, tool, panel or command name. Vendor names appear in this file ONLY as capture provenance.

mapping.title: Everything reachable from the top menu bar, including things reachable nowhere else
mapping.status: THIS PROPOSAL IS THE ANSWER TO THIS REQUIREMENT
mapping.how: proposal.full_tree carries 1,533 designed leaves plus 3,067 registry-budgeted expansion leaves across 15 Studio-contributed menus; proposal.menu_only_capabilities marks 375 nodes with no panel home; palette_relationship makes the menu a DERIVED VIEW of one command registry so nothing can be reachable in one surface and missing from another; context_gating.gating_rules.rule_5 forbids context-menu-only commands.

mapping.title: No persona toggle
mapping.status: PARTIALLY IN TENSION - see open_questions OQ-8
mapping.how: context_gating.gating_rules.rule_3 forbids task mode from changing which menu items exist or are enabled, which is the strong form of the operator's requirement applied to the menu bar. WORKSPACE > Task Mode exists at all only because Master Spec [STU-UNI-002] mandates task modes for panel layout and tool prominence. That is the tension, and it is the operator's to settle.

mapping.title: Panels dock to any of four edges, tabbed, user-reorganisable
mapping.how: WORKSPACE > Panels is an expansion node over that agent's 75-to-84 distinct panels. This proposal owns the menu toggles only, not the dock model.

mapping.title: Tooltips wherever possible
mapping.how: Every menu leaf carries a tooltip generated from the captures per the tools-and-tooltips deliberation's tooltip_data_contract, never hand-written. Disabled leaves additionally carry their machine-readable disabled_reason code (context_gating.gating_rules.rule_2), which is more than any source suite offers.

mapping.title: Arbitrary windows with tabs; documents and projects as tabs
mapping.how: WORKSPACE > Arrange Documents carries the menu commands (New Window, Tile, Consolidate, Move Document to Pane, Split Document View). Replacing the hard-coded 2x2 in split_layout.rs with egui_tiles is SAD-005, a prerequisite microtask this proposal depends on but does not specify.

mapping.title: Notes embeds Studio documents
mapping.how: FILE > Open From Asset Library and FILE > Browse Assets are the cross-module seam. The Notes-side attachment flow routes through navigation_bus.rs per SAD-003 and belongs to a different deliberation.

mapping.title: Scope boundary is by document type, not by application
mapping.how: All seven shapes the operator named (raster, vector, layout, motion, video, web, photo-catalog) are preserved by name in context_gating.the_seven_shapes_the_operator_named. The refinement: they are CAPABILITY PROFILES over one StudioDocument, not seven document TYPES, because [STU-DOC-001] states there is no per-source-app document silo. A type enum would rebuild the seven-application silo inside one binary and would break [STU-DOC-004].

mapping.title: Whether disabled menu items stay visible and greyed, as Adobe does, or are hidden when out of context
mapping.status: THIS PROPOSAL ANSWERS IT - position taken, operator may overrule
mapping.answer: VISIBLE AND GREYED, ALWAYS, at every level including top-level menu titles. Never hidden. Four reasons, in context_gating.gating_rules.rule_1: (1) the operator's own premise that the menu is the exhaustive index, and an index whose entries disappear is not an index; (2) [STU-MDL-002] requires every operator-visible surface to expose a stable AccessKit author_id, and a hidden node has no target, so Argus cannot inspect what is not rendered; (3) a bar that never moves is learnable, documentable in the UserManual (14.22) and scriptable by position; (4) field precedent - Dreamweaver's 2,176 invocable entries carry enabler_js predicates such as dw.canClipCut(), i.e. ENABLEMENT predicates, not visibility predicates. Studio goes one step past Adobe by attaching a machine-readable disabled_reason code readable from the tooltip, the AccessKit node AND the command API, so a greyed item answers 'why' instead of staying silent.
mapping.the_cost_the_operator_should_weigh: 19 fixed top-level titles, roughly 135 characters of chrome. Width is handled by an order-preserving overflow chevron that still emits every title into the AccessKit tree - a rendering concern, never a removal.

mapping.title: The reference tree is feat/WP-KERNEL-012, not main
mapping.status: APPLIED AS A CORRECTION TO THIS FILE
mapping.how: All three native-shell files were re-read from ../wtc-native-editors-v1. The shell menu bar has EIGHT menus at NodeId 92..=99, not six at 92..=97, and the command catalog is 93 commands across three tables, not 26 across two. See palette_relationship.existing_code_read.correction.

mapping.title: split_layout.rs and module_switcher.rs are React ports to be replaced
mapping.how: Studio module menus bind to the FOCUSED PANE's module. SAD-005 records that module_switcher.rs currently REWRITES the active pane's tab list on module switch and that MODULE_DEFINITIONS[Studio] is the Lab entry reordered. Until that is replaced with a viewport swap over live state (OUI-001), 'the Studio module has focus' is not a stable predicate and the module-menu insertion rule cannot be implemented correctly. See risks R-12.

mapping.title: Panels un-merge
mapping.how: WORKSPACE > Panels is sized at 84, not 75 and not the registry's 814.

mapping.title: No new router
mapping.how: The menu adds no navigation machinery. Menu leaves dispatch command ids; cross-surface navigation targets resolve through the existing navigation_bus.rs and loom_address.rs layers.

mapping.title: The capability registry merges on normalised name alone, conflating unrelated capabilities
mapping.status: APPLIED AS A CORRECTION TO TWO EXPANSION NODES; STILL AN OPEN RISK FOR THE REST
mapping.how: WORKSPACE > Tools now uses the tools agent's 353 rebuilt-from-source tools rather than the registry's 1,270 kind=tool rows, and WORKSPACE > Panels uses 84 rather than 814. Every OTHER expansion node in this proposal still draws on the registry and therefore inherits the overcount risk. See open_questions OQ-9 and risks R-9.

per_app_menu_shape.shape_finding: InDesign is TYPE-heavy and OBJECT-heavy. Its two biggest menus (Type 61, Object 53) are 46% of its main-menu leaf paths. Layout, the menu that names the application's whole purpose, has only 9 leaf paths because the page work lives in the Pages panel.

per_app_menu_shape.capture_method: lenient tag scan of Configuration/Menus/menus.xml + Custom Sets; app_launched=false
per_app_menu_shape.shape_finding: Dreamweaver's Insert menu alone carries 399 invocable entries — the single largest menu in any captured application, 41% of its entire main menu bar. Find is promoted to its OWN top-level menu with 16 items, which no other captured app does. 88 of its 89 menubars are context menus, so 1,210 of its 2,176 invocable entries are unreachable from the menu bar.

per_app_menu_shape.capture_method: PremiereData parse of .kys files + .eve menu scripts; app_launched=false
per_app_menu_shape.shape_finding: Premiere is the only captured app that promotes Markers (30 commands) to a top-level menu, and the only one whose main menu is DEEPER than 3 levels below the title (File reaches 4). 340 of its 1,491 commands exist only in the executable with no menu label at all — 23% of the command surface is menu-unreachable. Its 82 command namespaces are effectively a second, richer taxonomy than the 11-menu bar.

per_app_menu_shape.capture_method: binary parse of the shipped shortcut table; modifier bit meanings DERIVED and calibrated against 14 known shortcuts
per_app_menu_shape.not_captured_reason: illustrator_shortcuts.json is a flat command table keyed by command_id (e.g. 'pasteBack', 'transformagain', 'Adobe New Swatch Shortcut Menu'). It carries NO menu path field, so Illustrator's real menu-bar hierarchy cannot be asserted from this capture. Only the Effect menu hierarchy is recoverable, from illustrator_effects.json effect_menu_index.
per_app_menu_shape.shape_finding: Illustrator's captured surface is 611 menu commands vs 131 tool commands, and 499 of the 742 (67%) ship with NO keyboard shortcut. Its Effect menu is 9 groups / 67 items, of which Warp alone is 26 — nearly 40% of the whole Effect menu is one distortion family.

per_app_menu_shape.capture_method: UTF-8 XML parse of Locales/en_US/.../Default Keyboard Shortcuts.kys; Photoshop.exe NOT inspected
per_app_menu_shape.not_captured_reason: Verbatim from the capture's own unknowns[0]: 'No mapping exists in this install from a .kys command id (e.g. id 10 = New...) to a menu path (File > New...). The menu hierarchy is not present in any readable install file. UNRESOLVED.' unknowns[3] adds that Photoshop.exe was not inspected. The only .mnu file in the whole install is a 71-byte header naming one menu SET ('Color and Tonal Correction'), not a menu tree.
per_app_menu_shape.shape_finding: Photoshop is the application this proposal can say the least about structurally and the most about behaviourally. Its 5 dynamic commands (Vanishing Point, Liquify, Lens Correction, Camera Raw Filter, Wide Angle Correction) carry NO id attribute at all — they are modal workspaces resolved at runtime, which is precisely the class of capability that has no panel and exists only as a menu entry.

per_app_menu_shape.not_captured_reason: Only aftereffects_effects_catalogue.json and aftereffects_presets.json exist in installed_exports/aftereffects/offline/ as of this read. No menu or shortcut capture was present.
per_app_menu_shape.shape_finding: 481 effects in 36 categories is 7x Illustrator's 67 effect-menu items. Any single Studio Effects menu that lists effects flat is unusable; the family level is mandatory, and 106 of the 481 are preset-only pseudo-effects that belong under a preset browser, not the effect list.

per_app_menu_shape.capture_method: catalog schema + module SQL recovery; app_launched=false
per_app_menu_shape.not_captured_reason: No menu or shortcut capture exists for Lightroom Classic in installed_exports/lightroom_classic/offline/.
per_app_menu_shape.shape_finding: The captured Lightroom surface is a CATALOG schema, not a menu. 19 collections tables + 19 metadata tables + 6 keyword tables describe an asset-library product. Under the greenroom sprint contract's operator decision, that surface belongs to CKC (WP-KERNEL-005), not to the Studio menu bar. Only the 7 develop tables map into Studio (DOCUMENT > Develop).

per_app_menu_shape.shape_finding: Figma contributes a node/property model, not a menu shape. Its 40 node types map onto StudioLayer kinds; its component/variant/variable API maps onto the OBJECT > Component and COLOR > Colour Variables branches.

divergences.axis: The container menu (what holds the content)

source_variants.photoshop: Image (NOT_CAPTURED; documented externally as image/canvas/mode ops)

divergences.studio_resolution: ONE menu named DOCUMENT. It absorbs Layout, Sequence, Image, Composition and Site-tree structure because [STU-DOC-001] declares ONE StudioDocument whose containers (artboard / page_spread / timeline / board / site_tree) are a property of the document, not a property of the application. 170 explicit leaves, 27 submenus.
divergences.rule: DOCUMENT = whole-document scope. OBJECT = selection scope. That single line resolves every container-menu naming fight in the five sources.

divergences.axis: The selection-target menu (Layer vs Object vs Item vs Clip)

source_variants.indesign: Object (53 leaf paths, 19 shortcut sub-categories, 25 submenus)

divergences.studio_resolution: ONE menu named OBJECT, with Layer, Clip, Frame, Table and Component as SECOND-level branches. This is the largest Studio menu: 292 explicit leaves + 311 registry-expansion leaves, 40 submenus.
divergences.rule: A StudioLayer's kind selects which OBJECT branches enable; it never selects which menu you open.

source_variants.photoshop: Filter (NOT_CAPTURED) — historically destructive, plus Smart Filters
source_variants.affinity: Live Filters panel + Layer Effects panel

divergences.studio_resolution: ONE menu named EFFECTS. Spec 14.9 §1 already makes the non-destructive effect model normative and [STU-AUT-001] puts StudioEffectStack, StudioAdjustment, StudioLiveFilter and StudioBlendMode in ONE `effect` command family. The destructive/non-destructive split becomes a per-application option, not a menu boundary.
divergences.rule: Destructive application is a MODE of an effect, never a separate menu. Adjustments live here too, not under a document/image menu, because the command family says so.

source_variants.photoshop: Select (NOT_CAPTURED but its .kys carries All/Deselect/Inverse/Colour Range as application-scope commands)
source_variants.indesign: no Select menu — selection lives under Edit and Object>Select

divergences.studio_resolution: PROMOTE to top-level SELECT (59 explicit leaves, 6 submenus). Justification: StudioSelectionSet is a first-class canonical primitive in [STU-DOC-002] and `selection` is its own command family in [STU-AUT-001]. Burying it under Edit contradicts the primitive set.

divergences.axis: Colour has no top-level menu anywhere

source_variants.all_five: colour is scattered: Edit>Colour Settings, View>Proof Setup, Image>Mode, Swatches panel flyout, Window>Colour

divergences.studio_resolution: CREATE a top-level COLOR menu (78 explicit leaves + 110 expansion leaves, 11 submenus). Justification: color is the SECOND-LARGEST registry domain at 7,009 rows (17.2% of all 40,798 capabilities), and [STU-UNI-003] mandates ONE colour pipeline across all task modes. Scattering it across four menus is exactly the findability failure this proposal exists to fix.
divergences.cost: This is a deliberate break from all five sources. Users trained on Adobe will look under Edit and View first; both keep alias entries pointing at the COLOR leaves.

source_variants.dreamweaver: _Insert — 399 invocable entries, 12 submenus, the largest single menu in the whole capture set
source_variants.indesign: insertion is scattered: Type>Insert Special Character, Type>Insert White Space, Type>Insert Break, Object>Insert Anchored Object, Table>Insert
source_variants.premiere: insertion is an edit action on the timeline, not a menu

divergences.studio_resolution: CREATE a top-level INSERT menu (70 explicit + 367 expansion leaves). Everything that ADDS new content to the document is here, whatever the domain: layers, shapes, text, tables, page elements, components, media, web elements, board objects, snippets.
divergences.rule: INSERT creates; OBJECT modifies what exists.

source_variants.premiere: &Markers as its own top-level menu, 30 commands, 5 submenus
source_variants.indesign: Position Marker under Edit; Unicode Markers under Type

divergences.studio_resolution: Fold into MOTION > Markers (66 registry-expansion leaves). A dedicated top-level Markers menu cannot be justified at 66 leaves when MOTION already needs to exist.

source_variants.dreamweaver: Fin_d as its own top-level menu, 16 items

divergences.studio_resolution: Fold into EDIT > Find & Replace (13 leaves). Dreamweaver's promotion of Find to top level is an artefact of it being a code editor; the shell's own search rail (search_rail.rs) and the command palette already cover cross-project search.

Split three ways: authoring content -> INSERT > Web Element (282 expansion leaves); code-surface operations -> a new top-level CODE menu (59 explicit leaves, 8 submenus); site/server lifecycle -> FILE > Site Management and FILE > Publish.
divergences.cost: CODE is the most contestable of the 15 Studio-contributed menus — see risks R-6.

source_variants.dreamweaver: _Tools>Comman_ds, backed by 264 scripted command surfaces in Configuration/Commands
source_variants.affinity: macros + batch only, no scripting API at all

divergences.studio_resolution: CREATE a top-level AUTOMATE menu (82 explicit leaves, 10 submenus). It also carries the Handshake-native Command API and Model Lane branches that no source suite has.
divergences.rule: [STU-AUT-001] one typed command contract; the menu is one of its three callers, so the automation surface belongs in the menu bar, not in a panel flyout.

source_variants.illustrator: 131 tool commands in the shortcut table with NO menu path
source_variants.photoshop: 92 tool entries, 18 of them with no key at all, none in a menu
source_variants.premiere: cmd.tools.* namespace, 29 commands, not in the main menu

divergences.studio_resolution: PUT EVERY TOOL IN THE MENU under WORKSPACE > Tools (1,270 registry-expansion leaves). No source suite does this.
divergences.rationale: The operator's premise is that the menu is the exhaustive index. A tool that exists only as a toolbox icon and an unlabelled letter key is not indexed. [STU-MDL-006] also forbids capabilities with no model path; giving every tool a menu node gives every tool a stable command_id and a stable AccessKit author_id at once.

architectural_position.one_menu_bar_two_owners: Studio does NOT get its own menu bar. The native shell's existing bar (top_menu_bar.rs in feat/WP-KERNEL-012: EIGHT menus FILE, EDIT, VIEW, GO, RUN, HELP, EDITORS, OPERATOR at fixed AccessKit NodeId 92..=99) stays, and Studio CONTRIBUTES: items into FILE, EDIT, VIEW and HELP, plus 11 new module menus inserted between VIEW and GO while a pane showing ModuleId::Studio has focus. EDITORS and OPERATOR are untouched.
architectural_position.why: A second menu bar would duplicate FILE and EDIT, break the shell's fixed-NodeId identity contract, and make GO and RUN unreachable while designing. See open_questions OQ-3.
architectural_position.one_document_not_seven: [STU-DOC-001] declares one StudioDocument with layer kinds and container kinds. There is therefore no 'raster menu bar' or 'layout menu bar' — there is one bar whose items gate on a declared capability profile.
architectural_position.the_index_promise: Every capability is reachable from this menu tree, including capabilities that also have panels, tool option bars or context menus. Panels, option bars and context menus are PROJECTIONS of menu leaves, never homes for capabilities the menu lacks.

top_level_menus.label: FILE
top_level_menus.rationale: Document lifecycle and everything that crosses the process boundary: create, open, save, place, import, export, publish, package, preflight, print, version history. Already exists in the native shell as MenuId::File; Studio contributes into it rather than creating a second File menu.

top_level_menus.label: EDIT
top_level_menus.rationale: Reversible operations on the current state plus the application's own configuration: history, clipboard, find/change, spelling, tracked changes, notes, assignments, preferences, keyboard and menu customisation, capability grants. Exists in the shell as MenuId::Edit.
absorbs_source_menus: indesign:Edit (32 leaf paths, 11 shortcut sub-categories) + ChangesMenu + NotesMenu

top_level_menus.label: VIEW
top_level_menus.rationale: Everything that changes what the operator sees without changing the document: zoom, screen mode, display quality, proofing, rulers, guides, grids, snapping, extras, rotation, code-view options, live preview, video overlays, story editor. Exists in the shell as MenuId::View.

top_level_menus.label: DOCUMENT
top_level_menus.rationale: Whole-document scope. Setup, size, colour mode, bit depth, and every container the StudioDocument can declare: artboards, pages and spreads, parent pages, sections, liquid layout, long-document apparatus, timelines, boards, site trees, develop sessions, grids, fonts, accessibility. Replaces four differently-named container menus with one.

top_level_menus.label: SELECT
top_level_menus.rationale: The StudioSelectionSet primitive gets its own menu because it is a canonical primitive ([STU-DOC-002]) and its own command family ([STU-AUT-001]). Select all/by/modify/from, content-aware selection, selection sets, selection navigation, isolation, quick mask.

top_level_menus.label: OBJECT
top_level_menus.rationale: Selection scope. Transform, arrange, align, group, lock, hide, layers, masks, paths, booleans, shapes, frames and fitting, tables, components, auto layout, constraints, layout grids, blends, procedural constructs, clips, styles and appearance. The largest Studio menu, absorbing four source apps' differently-named object menus.
absorbs_source_menus: indesign:Object (53 leaf paths, 19 shortcut sub-categories, 25 submenus) + Table (18 leaf paths)

top_level_menus.label: TYPE
top_level_menus.rationale: The typography engine surface. Font, size, character, paragraph, OpenType, variable fonts, styles, special characters, white space, breaks, glyphs, type on a path, threading, conversion, story, CJK and complex scripts. InDesign's biggest menu and the registry's highest menu-kind domain after cross_cutting.
absorbs_source_menus: indesign:Type (61 leaf paths, 20 shortcut sub-categories, 15 submenus) + Japanese Typography (5 categories)

top_level_menus.label: COLOR
top_level_menus.rationale: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE: no source suite has a top-level colour menu, and that is the problem. Colour settings, working spaces, policies, document profile, proofing, swatches, spot colour and ink, separations and output, recolour, LUTs, picker, gradients and patterns, colour variables. Justified by colour being 7,009 of 40,798 registry rows and by [STU-UNI-003]'s one-colour-pipeline mandate.

top_level_menus.label: EFFECTS
top_level_menus.rationale: One menu for what the sources split into Effect, Filter, Adjustments, Layer Style and Live Filters. Apply Effect (20 Handshake-native families over 984 registry effect rows / 481 After Effects effects / 67 Illustrator effect items), adjustments, layer effects, live filters, the effect stack, interactive effect workspaces, presets, rendering.

top_level_menus.label: MOTION
top_level_menus.rationale: Time and interaction. Playback, go-to, keyframes, markers, in/out, edit actions, tracks, transitions, speed and time, audio, captions, render and preview, motion presets, motion aids, and the whole prototyping surface. Named MOTION rather than Timeline because it covers both time-based animation and trigger-based interaction, which the sources split across three applications.

top_level_menus.label: INSERT
top_level_menus.rationale: Everything that ADDS content: layers, shapes, text, tables, page elements, components and library items, media, web elements, whiteboard objects, snippets, markers, special characters. Modelled on Dreamweaver's Insert menu, which at 399 invocable entries is the largest single menu in the entire capture set.
absorbs_source_menus: indesign:Type>Insert Special Character / Insert White Space / Insert Break + Table>Insert
premiere:insert media (bars, black video, counting leader)

top_level_menus.label: CODE
top_level_menus.rationale: Web-document authoring: view mode, source formatting, code editing, refactoring, style sheets, validation, assistance, server model. Scoped narrowly to web authoring; general text editing is delegated to the native shell's editor surface so Studio does not double-build an editor (STU-SECTION-003 no-double-features).

top_level_menus.label: AUTOMATE
top_level_menus.rationale: Actions, macros, batch, scripts, the typed Command API, data-driven graphics, plugins, the model lane, jobs, and find/change run as a batch. The automation domain is 1,261 registry rows and is almost entirely menu- and dialog-shaped: it has 287 command rows and 18 dialog rows but its panel presence is thin.

top_level_menus.label: WORKSPACE
top_level_menus.rationale: The Window menu, renamed because the shell already owns windows and panes. Task modes, every panel (814 registry panel rows), every tool (1,270 registry tool rows), panel layouts, toolbox, chrome, presence, document arrangement.

top_level_menus.label: GO
top_level_menus.rationale: Existing shell menu (top_menu_bar.rs MenuId::Go): Quick Switcher (Ctrl+P), Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P), pane navigation. Studio contributes nothing; navigating between panes and projects is a shell concern.

top_level_menus.label: RUN
top_level_menus.rationale: Existing shell menu (MenuId::Run): Swarm Board, Inference Lab, Flight Recorder, Terminal. Studio contributes nothing; its own job surface is AUTOMATE > Jobs, which is document-scoped rather than session-scoped.

top_level_menus.label: HELP
top_level_menus.rationale: Existing shell menu (MenuId::Help). Studio contributes the dual-audience Studio Manual (14.22), the Full Command Index, the keyboard shortcut reference, and the diagnostics surface required by [STU-QUIET-005] and HBR-VIS.

top_level_menus.label: EDITORS
top_level_menus.rationale: Existing shell menu added by WP-KERNEL-012 MT-035 (MenuId::Editors, NodeId 98): native-editor side panes (Outline, Relevant Memory, Outgoing Links, Stage, Sidebar, Daily Journal) plus Format Document, diagnostics navigation, Rename Symbol and Quick Fix. Studio contributes nothing; these are text-editor concerns and Studio must not double-build them (STU-SECTION-003). This menu is the reason Studio's CODE menu is scoped to web-document authoring only — see risks R-6 and open_questions OQ-5.

top_level_menus.label: OPERATOR
top_level_menus.rationale: Existing shell menu added by WP-KERNEL-012 (MenuId::Operator, NodeId 99): Command Palette, Swarm Board, Flight Recorder, Launch Model Session, User Manual, Settings. Studio contributes nothing; its own model-lane surface is AUTOMATE > Model Lane, which is document-scoped rather than session-scoped.

rule_1_nothing_is_ever_hidden.position: Every top-level menu title is ALWAYS present while the Studio module has focus, in a fixed order, and every item inside every menu is ALWAYS present. Inapplicable items are DISABLED, never removed.
why: The operator's premise is that the menu is the exhaustive index of the application. An index whose entries disappear is not an index.

[STU-MDL-002] requires every operator-visible surface to expose a stable author_id in the AccessKit tree. A hidden menu has no node and therefore no stable target; Argus cannot inspect what is not rendered.
A menu whose contents move between documents cannot be learned, cannot be documented in the UserManual (14.22), and cannot be scripted by position.

Adobe already greys rather than hides, and Dreamweaver ships the machinery for it: 2,176 of its flat_command_index entries carry an enabler_js predicate (e.g. dw.canClipCut()). The field precedent is enablement predicates, not visibility predicates.
rule_1_nothing_is_ever_hidden.the_cost_accepted: 19 top-level titles is wider than any source app (InDesign 12, Premiere 11, Dreamweaver 10). Width is handled by an overflow chevron that PRESERVES ORDER and still emits every title into the AccessKit tree; it is a rendering concern only, never a removal.

rule_2_the_enablement_predicate.shape: Every menu leaf declares `requires`, a conjunction of typed clauses. enabled = all clauses satisfied AND the caller holds the required capability grant ([STU-AUT-005]) AND no blocking lease is held by another actor ([STU-PAR-003]).
rule_2_the_enablement_predicate.the_thing_adobe_never_does: The reason code is machine-readable and is carried on the AccessKit node, shown in the tooltip, AND returned by the command API when a model calls a disabled command. Adobe greys an item and tells you nothing. Studio's greyed item answers 'why' in one hover and in one API call.
rule_2_the_enablement_predicate.not_implemented_yet_precedent: The existing native shell already does exactly this: top_menu_bar.rs renders leaves whose target is a future microtask as DISABLED with a disclosed reason in the tooltip, and command_registry.rs sets disabled:true on all 13 Editor commands until the editor pane lands. Studio extends the same convention, with NOT_IMPLEMENTED_YET carrying the owning MT id so the menu doubles as a live build-progress index.

rule_3_task_mode_never_gates_the_menu.position: Switching task mode (WORKSPACE > Task Mode: Photo / Vector / Layout / Design System / Motion / Web / Develop / Board) changes tool prominence and panel layout ONLY. It MUST NOT change which menu items exist, which are enabled, or where they sit.
rule_3_task_mode_never_gates_the_menu.why: [STU-UNI-002] states that switching mode changes tool prominence and panel layout only, and that document state, selection, colour and history are untouched. If mode also gated the menu, mode would become an application switch in disguise — precisely the architecture the unified suite exists to replace. Gating is a property of the DOCUMENT, not of the operator's current workspace.

rule_4_enable_by_promotion_not_by_refusa.position: When an item is disabled because a container or feature is absent but Studio could ADD it, the item stays disabled and a sibling 'Enable <feature> for this document…' item is enabled next to it.
rule_4_enable_by_promotion_not_by_refusa.example: In a page-layout document, MOTION > Keyframes is disabled with NO_SUCH_CONTAINER; MOTION > Timelines > New Timeline (in DOCUMENT) is enabled. Adding the timeline enables the whole MOTION branch without converting the document.
rule_4_enable_by_promotion_not_by_refusa.why: This is the concrete payoff of one unified document. Adobe's answer to 'I want to animate this layout' is 'open a different application and re-import'.

rule_5_context_menus_are_a_projection_ne.position: No command may exist ONLY in a context menu. Every context-menu entry is a reference to a menu-bar leaf id.
rule_5_context_menus_are_a_projection_ne.evidence: InDesign carries 448 leaf paths across its right-mouse roots (RtMouseText 64, RtMouseLayout 57, RtMouseTable 18 and 31 more) against 245 in its main menu. Dreamweaver has 88 context menubars against 1 main menubar, so 1,210 of its 2,176 invocable entries are context-only. Premiere's largest context menus (HandlerMonitor_Source 115 items, HandlerTimeline_AVClip 111) rival its whole View menu. This is the single biggest source of 'reachable only if you already knew' in the source suites.
rule_5_context_menus_are_a_projection_ne.consequence: The native shell already has context_menu.rs and context_menu_surfaces.rs; Studio's context menus are built by filtering the same registry, so a leaf cannot be added to a context menu without existing in the menu tree first.

palette_relationship.the_rule: ONE registry, TWO projections, ZERO drift. The menu tree is not a parallel structure that references commands; the menu tree IS a field on the command record.

new_fields.menu_path: &'static [&'static str] — e.g. ["OBJECT","Path","Offset Path…"]. Empty slice means palette-only.
new_fields.menu_order: u32 — position among siblings; separators are gaps in the sequence, not nodes.
new_fields.domain: the registry domain (one of the 17) — used for grouping, filtering and coverage assertions.
new_fields.capability: &'static str — the [STU-AUT-005] capability the caller must hold.
new_fields.menu_only: bool — true when no panel offers this capability.

palette_relationship.scale_warning: The existing palette filters 26 commands per frame with `filtered_commands()` allocating a fresh Vec per call, which its doc comment says is well under the red-team MC2 frame budget. At 6,247 commands that is no longer true. The palette needs a prefix/trigram index built once in the same OnceLock, and the menu tree must be built once, not per frame. This is a concrete, sized performance requirement, not a caveat.

the_measured_problem.method: Every bound chord was normalised to Ctrl/Alt/Shift + KEY across the four applications whose binding tables are machine-readable (Photoshop .kys, Illustrator binary shortcut table, Premiere .kys default_bindings_en, Dreamweaver active factory set 'Dreamweaver Standard'). InDesign ships 162 shortcut CATEGORIES in indesign_command_surface.json but no key values, so it is excluded from the collision counts. After Effects has no shortcut capture.
the_measured_problem.headline: Only 18 of 211 contested chords mean the same thing in two or more applications. 91% of the contested keyboard surface is in conflict. A naive union of the four default sets is not merely awkward, it is undefined for 193 chords.

meanings.premiere: New Bin / New Folder / titler font bold

cited_collisions.studio_ruling: Bold. TYPE > Character > Bold. Two of four sources already mean bold, and bold is the highest-frequency operation of the four. Colour Balance moves to Ctrl+Alt+B; Paste in Back moves to Ctrl+Shift+Alt+V; New Bin becomes a CKC command, not a Studio one.

Duplicate (EDIT > Duplicate). Deselect takes Ctrl+Shift+A, which Photoshop already uses for Deselect Layers and Illustrator for Deselect. Transform Again keeps Ctrl+Alt+T. Apply Default Video Transition keeps Ctrl+Alt+D but only in the timeline context.
cited_collisions.note: This is the single most contested chord in the corpus: four applications, four unrelated meanings, none of them wrong.

cited_collisions.studio_ruling: Merge Down (OBJECT > Layer > Merge Down). Highest-frequency meaning. Edit Original moves to Ctrl+Shift+E in the interop context; Insert Tag is CODE-context-scoped.
Layer via Copy (OBJECT > Layer > New > Layer via Copy). Join takes Ctrl+Alt+J, which no captured app uses.
Levels… (EFFECTS > Adjustments > Levels…). Loop is timeline-context-scoped and keeps Ctrl+L there — this is the first case where the CONTEXT rule, not the priority rule, resolves the conflict.
Curves… (EFFECTS > Adjustments > Curves…). Export Media becomes Ctrl+Shift+M; window minimise is an OS/shell concern, not a Studio binding.

Free Transform (OBJECT > Transform > Free Transform). Character panel moves to Ctrl+Alt+T… no — Ctrl+Alt+T is Transform Again; the Character panel takes Ctrl+Shift+Alt+C. Quick Tag Editor is CODE-context-scoped and keeps Ctrl+T there.
Hue/Saturation… (EFFECTS > Adjustments). Underline takes Ctrl+Shift+U. Preferences takes Ctrl+K, which two of four sources already use.

Italic. TYPE > Character > Italic, matching the Ctrl+B ruling so the bold/italic pair stays coherent. Invert takes Ctrl+Shift+I… which is Inverse Selection in Photoshop; Invert therefore takes Ctrl+Alt+I. Import takes Ctrl+Shift+I only in FILE context.
cited_collisions.note: Ctrl+I is the clearest demonstration that a global priority rule alone cannot resolve these: fixing Ctrl+I forces a cascade through Ctrl+Shift+I and Ctrl+Alt+I.

cited_collisions.studio_ruling: Preferences (EDIT > Preferences). Two of three agree. Add Edit takes Ctrl+K in the timeline context only.
Show Rulers (VIEW > Rulers & Measurement). Three of three agree on rulers; Premiere's second meaning loses.

This is not a cross-app conflict — it is a SHIPPED INTRA-APP DUPLICATE. illustrator_shortcuts.json duplicate_bindings has exactly one entry: modifiers_raw 192 (Ctrl+Alt), key_code 69 (E), commands ['Menus/Last Filter','Menus/exportForScreens']. the_18_agreeing_chords_frozen_as_the_spi.rule: These 18 were measured to carry the same meaning in two or more captured applications. They are FROZEN: they may not be rebound to a different command by any default set, any context, or any preset. An operator may still rebind them manually; a Studio-shipped set may not.

resolution_rules_in_priority_order.rule: FROZEN SPINE. The 18 measured-agreeing chords are immovable in shipped sets.

CONTEXT SCOPE BEFORE ARBITRATION. A chord may carry different meanings in different input contexts, and context is resolved before any global arbitration. This is field-standard, not an invention: Premiere ships 31 shortcut contexts (global 11,687 binding rows, project 1,843, titler 1,524, timeline 1,336, multicam 600); Photoshop ships 3 dispatch scopes (application, tool_palette, taskspace) and its capture explicitly says 'A Rust reimplementation must decide scope precedence explicitly'; Illustrator ships 2 contexts (global 217, text_editing 26); Dreamweaver ships 8 shortcutlists.
resolution_rules_in_priority_order.precedence: modal_workspace > panel_focus > text_editing > code_surface > timeline > develop > board > canvas > global. Most specific focused surface wins; the first context that binds the chord consumes it.

resolution_rules_in_priority_order.rule: TOOL LETTERS ARE ONE GLOBAL NAMESPACE. Unmodified letters select tools, everywhere, always. In a unified document a tool is cross-domain, so a letter cannot mean Brush in one mode and Ripple Edit in another. Photoshop's own capture reports 22 within-scope and 19 cross-scope bare-letter collisions and classifies them as 'tool_cycle_group' and 'cross_scope_reuse' by HEURISTIC, not from the file. Studio removes the ambiguity: one letter, one tool, and Shift+letter cycles the declared group.

DOMAIN WEIGHT BREAKS TIES. When two commands in the SAME context both want a chord, the one whose registry domain has more rows wins the bare chord and the other takes a modifier-extended chord. Domain weights from the registry: cross_cutting 8,357 > color 7,009 > effects 4,420 > layout 4,204 > vector 3,240 > interop 2,656 > typography 2,522 > raster 2,479 > design_system 1,511 > automation 1,261 > web 1,158 > video 693 > raw 398 > prototype 365 > motion 310 > document_model 183 > whiteboard 32.
resolution_rules_in_priority_order.why_weight_and_not_taste: It is measurable, reproducible and arguable against evidence. Any other tie-break is one person's habit.

resolution_rules_in_priority_order.rule: FREQUENCY OVERRIDE. Domain weight may be overridden for a command whose measured invocation frequency in the flight recorder is in the top 5% — but only by a recorded decision with the measurement attached, never silently.

NO SILENT SHADOWING. Assigning a chord that is already bound in the same context is a hard validator failure at build time, not a UI warning at runtime. Illustrator shipped exactly this defect (Ctrl+Alt+E, above).

ONE CHORD PER COMMAND IN A SHIPPED SET. Photoshop ships 8 commands with two chords each (Cut = Ctrl+X and F2; 100% = Ctrl+1 and Alt+Ctrl+0; Browse in Bridge = Alt+Ctrl+O and Shift+Ctrl+O). Alternates double the collision surface for no gain. Operators may add their own; a shipped set carries one.

PHYSICAL-LAYOUT INDEPENDENCE. Bindings are stored against a logical key id, resolved through the active layout at dispatch. Dreamweaver ships 23 adaptive keyboard layout sets and Premiere ships 10 physical keyboard layouts; neither would be needed if bindings were layout-independent from the start.

PORTABLE SETS. A shortcut set is a document-independent, importable, exportable, diffable artefact (EDIT > Keyboard & Menus). Premiere ships 62 .kys set files across languages and Dreamweaver ships 3 factory sets; Studio ships ONE default plus named migration sets.

open_questions.question: Does Studio own footage clip editing, or not?
open_questions.conflict: Master Spec 14.1 [STU-OVR-015] states that editing imported video footage as a clip-timeline is OUT of Studio scope and belongs to engine.director (Spec §11.8). The greenroom sprint contract (greenroom-sprint-contract.json, operator_decisions_20260903.app_scope_expansion_20260903.spec_conflict_to_resolve_in_fold_back) states that After Effects and Premiere coverage SUPERSEDES that clause and that the enrichment proposal must add motion/video/timeline domains.
open_questions.what_it_changes_in_this_proposal: MOTION > Edit Actions (15 leaves), MOTION > Tracks (9), MOTION > Captions (8), MOTION > Audio (9), OBJECT > Clip (18 + submenus) and the whole 'video' document shape. Roughly 60 explicit leaves plus the 342 video-domain registry rows.
open_questions.needs: Operator decision, then a Master Spec amendment through the CX-405/CX-406 gate.

open_questions.question: Is the shared asset library Loom or CKC?
open_questions.conflict: Spec 14.21 [STU-UNI-003] says 'ONE asset/library surface (Loom is the home for brushes, styles, palettes, components, export recipes, and placed assets — no Studio-private asset silo)'. The greenroom sprint contract operator_decisions_20260903.asset_library_owner says 'CKC (WP-KERNEL-005, VALIDATED) is the asset library and file manager for WP-KERNEL-STUDIO, WP-KERNEL-010 Tailor, and the future cui-studio'.
open_questions.what_it_changes_in_this_proposal: FILE > Open From Asset Library, FILE > Browse Assets, FILE > Place from Asset Library, INSERT > Insert from Library, OBJECT > Component > Publish to Library, and every '…Libraries…' leaf under COLOR. The menu labels are written CKC-neutral today, but the destination is undecided.
open_questions.needs: Operator decision before any library leaf is wired.

open_questions.question: Does the Studio menu bar REPLACE the shell menu bar's six menus while Studio has focus, or INSERT between them?
open_questions.this_proposal_assumes: Insert. Shell keeps FILE/EDIT/VIEW/GO/RUN/HELP at their existing fixed AccessKit NodeId band 92..=97 and Studio contributes items into FILE/EDIT/VIEW/HELP plus 11 new module menus in a new dynamic band between VIEW and GO.
open_questions.the_alternative: Replace: the shell menus vanish while Studio is focused. That would break the fixed-NodeId contract in top_menu_bar.rs (MENU_BAR_NODE_ID_BASE = 92, six ids, registered in DECLARED_IDENTITIES with a collision test) and would make GO, RUN, EDITORS and OPERATOR unreachable from the menu while a designer works.
open_questions.needs: A native-shell architecture decision; it changes the NodeId allocation strategy. WP-KERNEL-012 MT-035 already extended the fixed band once (EDITORS at 98, OPERATOR at 99) which is the precedent, but a fixed band cannot absorb per-module menus, so 11 Studio menus need a reserved range or a dynamic id scheme.

open_questions.question: What is the top-level menu order, and is it stable across document shapes?
open_questions.this_proposal_assumes: Fixed order FILE, EDIT, VIEW, DOCUMENT, SELECT, OBJECT, TYPE, COLOR, EFFECTS, MOTION, INSERT, CODE, AUTOMATE, WORKSPACE, GO, RUN, HELP, EDITORS, OPERATOR — never reordered, never reordered by task mode, never reordered by frequency.
open_questions.the_argument_against: 19 fixed titles is ~135 characters of chrome. A frequency- or profile-ordered bar would put the live menus first. Rejected because positional stability is what makes the bar scriptable and learnable, but the operator may weigh screen width differently.

open_questions.question: Does Studio's CODE menu own general text editing, or only web-document authoring?
open_questions.this_proposal_assumes: Web-document authoring only. The native shell already ships an editor surface (command_registry.rs EDITOR_COMMANDS, atelier module, Monaco integration in the React shell) and STU-SECTION-003 forbids double features.
open_questions.unresolved: Where does editing a .js or .css file that belongs to a Studio site actually happen — in the Studio CODE surface or in the shell editor with a Studio context? The seam is currently a single leaf, CODE > Open in Shell Editor.

open_questions.question: Photoshop, Illustrator, After Effects and Lightroom Classic menu hierarchies are NOT CAPTURED. Four of the nine ingested applications contributed no menu shape at all.
open_questions.impact: Every claim in this document about Photoshop's Image/Layer/Select/Filter menus, Illustrator's Object/Type/Select/Effect menus, After Effects' Composition/Layer/Animation menus and Lightroom's Library/Photo/Metadata menus is marked NOT_CAPTURED and is inferred from the command and effect tables only.
open_questions.closing_action: Photoshop's hierarchy is most likely in Photoshop.exe compiled resources (the capture's unknowns[3] says the binary was not inspected). Illustrator's is likely recoverable from the .aip plugin menu registrations — illustrator_effects.json already recovered the Effect menu hierarchy that way, from 105 plugins with menu registration.

open_questions.question: Should 'preset' and 'option' registry kinds (9,512 + 15,862 = 25,374 rows, 62% of the registry) ever be menu-reachable?
open_questions.this_proposal_assumes: No. Presets live in preset browsers reached from a '…Presets…' leaf; options live in the dialog or option bar of the command that owns them. Putting them in the menu would triple the tree for no findability gain.
open_questions.risk_if_wrong: If an operator expects to apply a named preset directly from a menu (as Lightroom's develop-preset list does), the answer is a dynamic expansion node under the owning branch, not a redesign.

open_questions.question: Does WORKSPACE > Task Mode survive OUI-004 (no persona toggle)?
open_questions.conflict: Master Spec 14.21 [STU-UNI-002] makes TASK MODES normative: 'Operator workflows are organized as workspace/persona-style TASK MODES over the SAME document and primitives - a photo/pixel mode, a vector/design mode, a page-layout mode, a design-system/prototyping mode, and a whiteboard mode.' Operator requirement OUI-004 says the opposite: 'Affinity swaps its entire interface between nine personas. The operator rejects this. Panels should be job-related and contextual; the whole UI must not switch modes.'
open_questions.what_this_proposal_did: Split the difference. WORKSPACE > Task Mode exists (8 modes, 9 leaves) because the spec mandates it, but context_gating.gating_rules.rule_3 forbids mode from changing ANY menu content or enablement. The menu bar is persona-free even if the panel layout is not.
open_questions.the_real_question_for_the_operator: If OUI-004 is meant literally - panels are contextual and there is no mode switch at all - then WORKSPACE > Task Mode should be DELETED and the 9 leaves removed, and [STU-UNI-002] needs a spec amendment. If task mode survives as a panel-layout preset only, it should probably be renamed (Panel Preset, Layout Preset) so it never reads as a persona.
open_questions.evidence_the_operator_already_cited: OUI-004's own evidence section: 1,096 capabilities are shared by two applications, 327 by three, 127 by four, 69 by five, 29 by six and 6 by seven. The same tool serves multiple document types, so gating behind a mode means implementing once and hiding repeatedly.

open_questions.question: How much of this proposal's item count is inflated by green-room defect GRD-001?
open_questions.the_defect: studio-architecture-decisions.json known_defects_in_this_green_room GRD-001: the cross-app capability registry merges rows on normalised name alone, conflating unrelated capabilities. The tools deliberation rejected the registry's kind=='tool' bucket entirely and rebuilt from per-app sources.
open_questions.measured_impact_where_it_has_been_checke: Tools: registry says 1,270, rebuild says 353 (a 3.6x overcount). Panels: registry says 814, dedup says 75-84 (a 9.7x overcount).
open_questions.unchecked_exposure: This proposal's remaining registry-derived expansion nodes total roughly 2,630 leaves - Effects 1,230, Web Element 282, Adjustments 246, Table 152, Align & Distribute 132, Export 123, Colour Assets 110, Import 105, Shapes 85, Markers 66, Keyframes 31, OpenType 24, Prototype Triggers 170. If those carry a comparable overcount, the true designed-plus-expanded total is materially below 4,600.
open_questions.needs: Either a registry fix (merge on normalised name PLUS domain PLUS kind, with a provenance-preserving audit trail) or a per-family rebuild-from-source pass like the tools agent's, before any expansion node becomes a microtask.

open_questions.question: Where does the Studio module menu band live in the AccessKit NodeId space?
open_questions.context: WP-KERNEL-012 assigns MENU_BAR_NODE_ID_BASE = 92 and fixed ids 92..=99 for eight menus, registered in DECLARED_IDENTITIES with a collision test. MT-035 extended the band by two for EDITORS and OPERATOR, which proves the band is extensible - but only for SHELL menus.
open_questions.the_problem: Studio's 11 module menus cannot take 100..=110 because 100 is the pane id base. Per-module menus are also not a fixed set: Tailor, CKC and future modules will each want their own.
options: reserve a per-module band (e.g. 200 + module_index*32 + menu_index)
derive module-menu ids from author_id strings in egui's hashed id space, as top_menu_bar.rs already does for dynamic LEAF nodes (menu.{menu}.{leaf})
keep a single fixed band and require modules to declare menus at compile time
open_questions.recommendation_from_this_proposal: The second option. top_menu_bar.rs already proves the pattern for leaves; extending it to module menu TITLES keeps the fixed band for the shell's eight and makes module menus additive without renumbering. But this is a native-shell decision, not a Studio one.

risks.risk: Menu-bar width. 19 top-level titles at ~7 characters each is roughly 135 characters of chrome. The shell already ships 8 of them in WP-KERNEL-012 (FILE EDIT VIEW GO RUN HELP EDITORS OPERATOR); Studio adds 11 more. It fits 1920px, is tight at 1440px and overflows at 1280px.
risks.mitigation: An overflow chevron that preserves order and still emits every title into the AccessKit tree (rendering-only, never removal). Abbreviated titles at narrow widths before overflow. Measure at 1280/1440/1920/2560 in the visual debugger before the tree is frozen.
risks.do_not: Do not solve width by hiding inapplicable menus. That trades a rendering problem for an index-stability problem, and it breaks [STU-MDL-002] stable targets.

risks.risk: 6,247 items is a maintenance surface. Hand-maintaining it drifts within one release.
risks.mitigation: The tree is DERIVED from the command registry (palette_relationship.step_2), not authored. The 1,533 explicit leaves in this proposal are the DESIGN, not the implementation artefact; the implementation adds menu_path to each AppCommand and folds. INV-1..INV-6 are compile-time or test-time assertions.

risks.risk: The palette's per-frame filter does not survive the scale increase. filtered_commands() allocates a fresh Vec and does a substring scan per call over the whole catalog; today that is 26 rows, at Studio scale it is 6,247.
risks.evidence: command_registry.rs doc comment: 'Allocates a fresh Vec<&AppCommand> per call; the palette calls it once per frame against the small static catalog (well under the red-team MC2 frame-time budget).'
risks.mitigation: Build a prefix/trigram index once in the same OnceLock; cap rendered rows; keep matches_query as the semantic definition and the index as its accelerator so the four existing tests stay valid.

risks.risk: Shortcut migration pain. 193 of 211 contested chords change meaning relative to at least one source app, so every migrating professional loses muscle memory somewhere.
risks.mitigation: Three named migration sets (Raster-Familiar, Vector-Familiar, Timeline-Familiar) plus a first-run chooser. The frozen 18-chord spine guarantees that Cut/Copy/Paste/Undo/Save/Open/Print/Close never move for anyone.

risks.risk: The COLOR top-level menu is unfamiliar. Every migrating user will look under Edit and View first and conclude the feature is missing.
risks.mitigation: Alias leaves in EDIT (Colour Settings…) and VIEW (Proof) that point at the COLOR leaves, marked alias_of so INV-2 still holds. The palette breadcrumb teaches the real location on every search.

risks.risk: The CODE menu double-builds the shell's editor. Handshake already has an editor surface; a Studio code editor is a second one, which STU-SECTION-003 forbids.
risks.mitigation: CODE is scoped to web-document authoring operations that act on the DOCUMENT (view mode, source formatting, validation, CSS rules, server model), not to text editing primitives. The seam is CODE > Open in Shell Editor. OQ-5 must be closed before CODE is implemented.

risks.risk: Four of nine applications contributed no menu capture, so the absorption claims for Photoshop, Illustrator, After Effects and Lightroom are structurally weaker than for InDesign, Dreamweaver and Premiere.
risks.mitigation: Every such claim in this document is explicitly marked NOT_CAPTURED with the capture's own reason quoted. Close by inspecting Photoshop.exe resources and the Illustrator .aip menu registrations (OQ-6).

risks.risk: Gating predicates become a second, hidden source of truth that disagrees with the engine. An item enables but the command then fails.
risks.mitigation: The `requires` clause set is the SAME predicate the command API evaluates for [STU-AUT-005] capability gating and for dry_run. INV-4 asserts one evaluation feeds both projections; a command whose dry_run fails while its menu leaf was enabled is a test failure, not a UI bug.

risks.risk: Registry expansion counts are estimates from keyword matchers, not curated leaf lists. WORKSPACE alone claims 2,084 expansion leaves (814 panels + 1,270 tools) and EFFECTS claims 1,230.
risks.mitigation: Every expansion node names its exact leaf_source query so the count is reproducible and falsifiable. These are SIZING figures for the design, and each expansion becomes a curated list at implementation time. The explicit 1,533 leaves are the part of this proposal that is asserted rather than estimated.
risks.honest_statement: Do not treat 6,247 as a committed item count. Treat 1,533 as designed and 4,714 as budgeted.

risks.risk: Adding menu_path to AppCommand changes a struct that four existing tests depend on and that the app.rs dispatch match consumes.
risks.mitigation: All new fields have defaults compatible with the existing 26 commands (empty menu_path = palette-only). The four tests in command_registry.rs (no-duplicate-ids, stable-static-slice, matches_query, app-enabled/editor-disabled) are unaffected by additive fields.

risks.risk: Context-scoped shortcuts are invisible. An operator presses Ctrl+L expecting Levels, is focused on the timeline, and gets Loop.
risks.mitigation: The active context is displayed in the status bar (WORKSPACE > Chrome > Status Bar) and every menu leaf shows its chord ONLY when that chord is live in the current context, greyed with the context name otherwise. This is more than any source app does; Premiere ships 31 contexts and surfaces none of them in the menu.

risks.risk: Studio menus appear in the shell's menu bar while a non-Studio module has focus, or vanish mid-interaction when focus moves.
risks.mitigation: Module menus are bound to the FOCUSED PANE's module (module_switcher.rs ModuleId::Studio), and the bar re-renders only on module change, never on pane hover. A menu that is open when focus changes stays open and completes its interaction against the document it was opened for.

risks.risk: This proposal's expansion counts inherit green-room defect GRD-001 everywhere they have not been independently rebuilt.
risks.evidence: Two nodes have been checked against rebuilt-from-source counts and both were badly inflated: tools 1,270 -> 353, panels 814 -> 84.
risks.mitigation: Every expansion node names its exact leaf_source query so the count is falsifiable, and the two corrected nodes carry an explicit `correction` field. Treat the 1,533 explicit leaves as designed and every expansion figure as an upper bound pending a per-family rebuild. See open_questions OQ-9.

risks.risk: This proposal was largely drafted against the `handshake_main` worktree before operator decision SAD-001 was read, and main is stale.
risks.what_was_wrong: Six shell menus instead of eight; NodeId band 92..=97 instead of 92..=99; a 26-command catalog across two tables instead of 93 across three; top_menu_bar.rs at 704 lines instead of 2,696; and no awareness that 012 already ships effective_disabled(cmd, ctx) - the exact context-gating mechanism this proposal proposes.
risks.mitigation: All three files were re-read from ../wtc-native-editors-v1 and every affected figure corrected; palette_relationship.existing_code_read.correction records what changed. Any FURTHER claim in this file about native-shell internals that is not in that section should be re-verified against 012 before it reaches a microtask.
risks.systemic_note: SAD-002 records the same failure mode happening once before in this workstream ('Reading main would have produced wrong architecture conclusions, and did once'). A deliberation agent that is given a corpus path but not the reference-tree decision will read the wrong tree by default.
